The company never uses the term \"operating margin\" for this ratio and presents no non-GAAP alternative (E-04 ng.measure: \"no non-GAAP measure is presented\").", "fraction_of_level_accounted": "Of the 23% operating margin, the cyclical mechanism (11) is the dominant one and plausibly accounts for most of the distance between the 11% reported for Q3 FY2024 and the 23% reported for Q3 FY2025 — call it roughly half to substantially all of the current level, a range I cannot narrow because the bundle contains no full-cycle operating-margin series; the capitalisation-and-deferral mechanism (10) — $1,294m of incentives netted against capital expenditure, $3.40bn of equipment not in service, $4.94bn of construction in progress — accounts for an unquantified but structurally growing further slice by keeping future depreciation out of the numerator; and the lease-classification mechanism (1) accounts for well under one percentage point ($89m of nine-month finance-lease interest sitting below the operating line, against $6,116m of nine-month operating income).", "answer": "FACT [E-04 ng.measure, status not_found]: "no non-GAAP measure is presented" in the 10-Q. FACT [MD&A]: "Operating income (loss) | 2,169 | 23% ... 719 | 11% | 6,116 | 23% | (218) | (1)%". INFERENCE: the ratio is GAAP-standard and the usual accrual tricks are, on this evidence, not what produced it — cash conversion (6), receivables (7), inventory (8), non-recurring gains (3) and asset sales (4) all come back clean, and the two identifiable one-off benefits ($200m patent cross-license gain, $987m from selling written-down inventory) sit in the FY2024 comparatives, not in the current numerator.

Three mechanisms are present, and they are not accounting mechanisms. First, cycle (11): the company attributes the margin to average selling prices, and the DRAM price move it reports for the nine months ("a high-40% range increase in average selling prices") exceeds the top of the five-year annual range it publishes in its own risk factors ("plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range"). FACT [annual history, fcff]: four of nine fiscal years negative. INFERENCE: 23% is a position in a price cycle, not a structural level, and the sequential ASP declines already disclosed for both DRAM and NAND are the first evidence of direction change. Second, deferral (10): $1,294m of government incentives netted against capital expenditure, $3.40bn of equipment not placed into service and $4.94bn of construction in progress mean the current numerator does not yet carry the depreciation of the capacity being built — and FACT [MD&A]: capex is guided at "approximately $14 billion" for FY2025 against "$10,199" spent in nine months. Third, and trivially, lease classification (1) moves a growing amount of lease cost below the operating line.

Two mechanisms I cannot clear or convict. FACT [declared absent inputs]: "E-09 was SKIPPED after five truncated runs (DX-96)". INFERENCE: reserve and provision movements (5) and accounting-estimate changes (9) are unexamined — and the estimate with the largest leverage on this metric, equipment useful life against "Depreciation expense and amortization of intangible assets | 6,203", is not disclosed in this filing at all. FACT [Contingencies]: a jury "found that Micron should pay $425 million ... and $20 million", and the company "cannot make a reasonable estimate of the potential loss"; no accrual is disclosed.

ASSUMPTION: that the FY2024 comparatives are the right benchmark for what "normal" looks like. They are a trough, not a mid-cycle period, so year-over-year improvement overstates the structural gain; a reader who rejects this should treat mechanism 11 as accounting for more of the level than I have allowed, not less."}
